bug_semantics: PluginImportGuard is a sys.meta_path hook plus a sys.modules hider that is supposed to block dangerous imports at plugin runtime. Its denylist is CWE-184-incomplete: ALWAYS_BLOCKED is only {ctypes, __builtin__, __builtins__} and CAPABILITY_GATED adds subprocess (always), os (always), and socket (NETWORK_ACCESS). _should_block_module() returns False for every other top-level name, so find_module()/find_spec() do not raise and hide_dangerous_modules() never removes those names from sys.modules. After 50bec5d the AST analyzer's DANGEROUS_MODULES independently treats sys, shutil, multiprocessing, importlib, pickle, shelve, pty, fcntl, pwd, grp, signal, resource, pipes, popen2, and platform as never-importable; an attacker who bypasses that static pass (string obfuscation, encoding, or __import__ indirection) can therefore import those modules at runtime and reach arbitrary code execution (pickle.__reduce__, importlib, sys.modules, shutil, multiprocessing). Direct `import pickle`/`import sys` is the sink; AST is only the bypassable outer check.
